Photograph: Zsolt Szigetváry/EPA View image in fullscreen Demonstrators at a ‘We stand with CEU’ protest in Budapest in 2018. Photograph: Zsolt Szigetváry/EPA Hungary University hounded out of Hungary by Orbán reaches out to new government Prospect of partial return to Budapest by Central European University suggests confidence in Hungary’s future Jennifer Rankin in Brussels Sat 14 Nov 2026 00.00 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 00.02 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A university that Viktor Orbán tried to chase out of Hungary is open to expanding its presence in Budapest, in a mark of confidence in the country’s democratic future. Carsten Q Schneider, the interim president and rector of Central European University (CEU), said it was interested in increasing its programmes in Budapest, as long as this did not damage the student experience. So far the CEU has not held formal talks with Hungary’s new government, which has promised to restore academic freedom, “but our hand is reaching out, their hand is reaching out – it is just that they have many things to do ”, the academic told the Guardian.
